content: SHAP is consistently treated as a post-hoc, model-agnostic analysis stage that runs strictly after a model is trained and validated -- never embedded inside model training code. Standard placement: a separate interpretability module/script that loads a fitted model + the feature matrix, selects an explainer type (TreeExplainer for tree ensembles, LinearExplainer for linear/GLM models, KernelExplainer as a slower model-agnostic fallback), computes SHAP values, and produces summary/dependence plots. Because SHAP's efficient explainers target tree or linear scikit-learn-style estimators, applying it to a linearmodels PanelOLS fixed-effects result requires either wrapping the fitted model's predict step in a scikit-learn-compatible function for KernelExplainer/LinearExplainer, or running SHAP against a parallel scikit-learn model (e.g. RandomForest/GradientBoosting fit on the same panel-flattened features) as a complementary variable-importance check rather than on the panel model directly.
